title: Road to Vegas Is Set: Rookie Noah Lee Leads Bull Riders Into the 2026 NFR as Steer Roping Crowns Its Champion This Week
excerpt: The 2026 Wrangler National Finals Rodeo field is set for Dec. 3-12 in Las Vegas, with Texas rookie Noah Lee leading the bull riding standings, while Cole Patterson chases a fifth steer-roping world title this week in Kansas.
content:
The field for the 2026 Wrangler National Finals Rodeo is set. After the PRCA regular season closed Sept. 30, the top 15 in each event qualified for 10 go-rounds at the Thomas & Mack Center in Las Vegas, Dec. 3-12, 2026.

In bull riding, rookie Noah Lee of Mineral Wells, Texas, leads the world with $405,040.61 — a first-time NFR qualifier who also leads the Resistol Rookie race. Tristen Hutchings ($328,763.60) and Luke Mackey ($280,145.48) follow. In tie-down roping, Riley Webb leads all NFR qualifiers in earnings at $345,248.98, ahead of Haven Meged ($271,126.17).

Barrel racing is the tightest race at the top: Hayle Gibson-Stillwell leads at $218,455.50, with Emily Beisel at $214,122.83 and Carlee Otero at $202,388.99, and only about $90,000 separates No. 1 from No. 15. This is the first year the NFR pays eight places per round instead of six.

One championship will not be decided in Las Vegas. The breakaway roping final moves to Fort Worth, with the top 15 headed to the Wrangler WPRA National Breakaway Finals at Will Rogers Coliseum, Dec. 18-19, under a new three-year agreement. Cheyanne McCartney leads at $196,883.54, ahead of Hali Williams ($194,090.36) and Josie Conner ($190,596.82). Six Resistol rookies qualified for their first NFR, including Texas’ own Amy Ohrt of Victoria, the breakaway rookie leader at $70,993, and Morgan Bagnell, the barrel racing rookie leader at $61,665.

Before Las Vegas, a champion is crowned this week. The National Finals Steer Roping runs Friday and Saturday, Nov. 13-14, at Kansas Star Arena in Mulvane, Kansas, at 7 p.m. CT each night. Cole Patterson enters atop the standings at $120,826, chasing his fifth world championship and fourth in a row, wearing the No. 1 back number for the fifth time in six years. Taylor Santos ($108,064) and Riley O’Rourke ($89,658) are next.

In bull riding’s team format, the Nashville Stampede became the first team in PBR Teams history to repeat as champions, beating the Arizona Ridge Riders 356.45-268.35 in the championship game Sunday, Nov. 8, at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. Arizona’s Eduardo Aparecido was named Championship MVP. Nashville’s first title came in 2022.

The NFR field was settled at the Governor’s Cup in Sioux Falls in late September, where final-round winners each earned $34,000 — including Noah Lee’s 91-point bull ride and Andrea Busby’s barrel run that jumped her from No. 19 to No. 14.

Sources: Cowboy+, Oct. 20, 2026 (updated Nov. 5); PRCA PRORODEO Sports News, Nov. 6, 2026; PRCA.com, Nov. 10, 2026; PBR.com, Nov. 8, 2026; WPRA.com; Cowgirl Magazine, Oct. 12, 2026.
